title: RICE-PO: Turning Retrieval Interactions into Credit Signals for Reasoning Agents
claim: Credit for latent reasoning is assigned by anchoring on uncertain executable actions, testing counterfactual branches, and gating propagation on reliability.
layout: Top multi-round trajectory strip above three lettered panels A/B/C, left-to-right
description: A wide figure with two tiers. The top banner shows an agent loop. A query and initial documents feed Round 1, Round 2 and Round t. Each round has an orange think box labelled latent, a teal summary box labelled executable, and a document icon for the retriever response. A yellow dashed box marks the high-entropy anchor summary in Round 2. The rounds end in a Combine advantages box (A_total = w_t A_sum) and then Policy update. Below are three bordered panels. Panel A (purple) is a table of candidate summaries with entropy bars; the top-entropy rows are outlined in orange. Panel B (blue) is a tree from anchor history h_t into the original branch and K alternative branches, each with an NDCG@10 score, plus influence and residual-stability boxes. Panel C (green) shows gate logic (influence high, residual variance low, gate w open or closed) and token rows for other, summary and think tokens with their advantage terms.
caption: Overview of RICE-PO. The agent generates latent reasoning spans and executable summaries across multiple retrieval rounds. RICE-PO selects high-entropy summary anchors, estimates local influence and residual stability through counterfactual branches, and propagates summary-level credit to reasoning tokens only when the signal is reliable.
abstract: Retrieval is increasingly moving from one-shot matching toward interactive reasoning, where language agents iteratively inspect evidence, reformulate queries, and search again. Training such agents raises a credit-assignment challenge: executable actions such as queries or summaries can be directly evaluated by the retriever, while latent reasoning steps are not directly observable and only affect future executable actions. This asymmetry makes outcome-level reward assignment unreliable, as the same final reward may credit reasoning steps that did not actually shape retrieval success. We propose RICE-PO, a critic-free policy optimization framework that converts retrieval interactions into localized learning signals. RICE-PO selects high-uncertainty executable actions as anchors, evaluates local counterfactual branches using retrieval metrics, and propagates credit to latent reasoning steps only when reasoning-to-action influence is strong and future residual effects are stable. On BRIGHT and BEIR, RICE-PO consistently outperforms prompt-based agents and group-based RL baselines under the same retriever setting. These results show that the structure of agent-environment interaction itself can provide useful supervision for training reasoning-based retrieval agents.
